This performance was so goated that most people believed that Leonardo DiCaprio was actually mentally disabled.⁣ 👀 
⁣
Leonardo DiCaprio played the part of Arnie Grape so well that when he showed up for the film’s premiere, most people were shocked and astonished to learn that the 19 year old actor was not actually mentally disabled. According to Leo playing Arnie Grape was “the most fun I’ve ever had.”⁣
⁣
He improvised many of Arnie’s quirky behaviors, like randomly putting his head under water or climbing objects. To prepare, he studied videos of people with developmental disabilities and spent time with them to ensure an authentic portrayal. When getting into character, Leo remarked of it, “I had to really research to get into the mind of somebody like that. I spent a few days at a home for mentally unstable teens. We just talked and I watched their mannerisms. People have these expectations that mentally retarded children are really crazy, but that isn’t so. It’s refreshing to see them, because everything’s so new to them.”⁣
⁣
Furthermore Martin Scorsese first became aware of young Leo after seeing him in this film one night when he was watching it on TV. That discovery eventually led to one of Hollywood’s most iconic actor-director collaborations, beginning with Gangs of New York (2002) and continuing through films such as The Aviator, The Departed, Shutter Island, The Wolf of Wall Street, and Killers of the Flower Moon.⁣
⁣
